chapters.title: KHAZARIAN HISTORY — THE COMPLETE DOCUMENTED RECORD

content.text: The Khazar Khaganate was a Turkic-speaking steppe confederation that
operated as a major political power in the North Caucasus region from
approximately the 7th to the 10th centuries CE. What follows is the
documented record — distinguished at every point between what is
supported by primary sources and what is argued or hypothesized.
Geographic Territory and Political Centers
Core territory: the North Caucasus and Lower Volga region, Western
Kazakhstan steppe, Southern Russia, and parts of Ukraine. Primary
capitals: Itil, located near the Volga delta, functioning as the main
commercial and administrative center; and Sarkel, a fortress on the Don
River built with the assistance of Byzantine engineers, documented in
Byzantine imperial records and confirmed archaeologically.
Key sites: Sarkel fortress (Byzantine-engineered, excavated by Soviet
archaeologists in the 1930s-1950s before being submerged by the
Tsimlyansk Reservoir — photographic records exist in Soviet
archaeological archives); Itil at the Volga delta (not yet definitively
excavated but referenced in multiple independent Arabic and Byzantine
primary sources). Material culture at excavated Khazar sites is Turkic
steppe in structure — not Levantine or Semitic. This is a documented
archaeological finding relevant to the question of biological Israelite
origin.
Source: Golb, Norman and Pritsak, Omeljan — Khazarian Hebrew Documents
of the Tenth Century (Cornell University Press, 1982) · Byzantine
imperial records documenting Sarkel construction
Political Structure — Dual Rulership

content.heading: The Khazars operated a dual rulership model documented in multiple
paragraphs: independent Arabic sources: a Khagan — a sacral or symbolic ruler whose
person was treated as ritually significant but who held limited active
authority — and a Bek (also called the Khagan Bek) — the military and
administrative authority who exercised effective governance. This
structure is consistent with other documented Turkic steppe
confederations of the period and is confirmed independently in the
accounts of Ibn Fadlan, Al-Masudi, and Byzantine imperial records.

content.heading: The Khazar state functioned as a commercial buffer between the Byzantine
paragraphs: Empire to the west, the Umayyad and Abbasid Caliphates to the south, and
the Slavic and Rus' polities to the north. Its economic significance was
primarily as a toll-collecting transit state: it controlled the Volga
trade route running from the Baltic south through the Caspian toward
Abbasid lands, and the Don-Dnieper routes toward the Black Sea and
Byzantium. Arabic geographers Ibn Khordadbeh and Al-Masudi document the
Volga route and the Khazar customs-collection apparatus in their primary
geographic works.

content.heading: The Khazar ruling elite's adoption of Judaism is attested in multiple
paragraphs: independent primary sources. The Khazar Correspondence — a series of
letters between Hasdai ibn Shaprut, a Jewish physician in the court of
the Umayyad Caliph in Cordoba (Spain), and King Joseph of Khazaria,
approximately 960 CE — is the most direct primary documentation. King
Joseph writes explicitly in this correspondence that his people descend
from Togarmah, son of Gomer, son of Japheth — the genealogical line of
Genesis 10:3, which places the Khazar ancestral lineage in the northern
European-Anatolian branch, not in the Semitic lineage of Abraham. He
describes the conversion as a historical event, not an ancestral
identity.

content.text: Arabic chroniclers Al-Masudi (Muruj adh-Dhahab) and Ibn Fadlan (Risala,
documenting his 921-922 CE embassy to the Volga Bulgars) both reference
a Jewish Khazar ruling class. Byzantine sources reference the Khazar
Kagan's Jewish identity in the context of diplomatic relations. The
Kuzari — a 12th century philosophical work by Judah Halevi — is
explicitly based on the Khazar conversion narrative, presenting it as a
historical event in which a Khazar king chose Judaism over Christianity
and Islam for reasons of theological neutrality between the two dominant
imperial religious blocs.

content.heading: What the primary sources support: the Khazar ruling class — not
paragraphs: necessarily the entire population — adopted a form of Judaism sometime
between the 8th and 9th centuries CE. The conversion was politically
strategic, positioning Khazaria as a neutral party between Christian
Byzantium and the Muslim Caliphate. What the primary sources do not
support: there is no primary source evidence that the entire Khazar
population converted. There is no evidence of prior Israelite biological
descent among the Khazars before conversion. There is no evidence of
preserved pre-conversion Israelite ritual continuity in Khazar culture.

content.text: Source: Khazar Correspondence — Schechter Text, Cambridge University
Library · Firkovich Collection, St. Petersburg National Library · Ibn
Fadlan — Risala (921-922 CE) · Al-Masudi — Muruj adh-Dhahab · Golb and
Pritsak — Khazarian Hebrew Documents (Cornell, 1982)
▣ IMAGE: Khazar Correspondence — King Joseph's Letter to Hasdai ibn
Shaprut, c. 960 CE Archive: Cambridge University Library — Schechter
Geniza Fragment — loc.gov search: 'Khazar Correspondence schechter'
Note: Primary source in which King Joseph explicitly states Khazar
ancestry from Togarmah (Japheth line), not from Abraham or the 12
tribes. Public domain.

content.heading: The Khazar state participated in the medieval Eurasian slave trade as a
paragraphs: transit and taxation state. This is documented in Arabic geographic
sources. Ibn Khordadbeh describes multilingual Jewish merchants
(Radhanites) operating routes from Western Europe through Khazaria to
Central Asia and India. The mechanism: Khazaria imposed customs duties
on goods transiting its territory — including enslaved persons. The
supply zones for enslaved persons moving through Khazar territory were
the Slavic territories to the north and west (hence the etymology of the
English word slave, from Slavic), steppe and forest peoples, and
Caucasian populations. The Khazar state profited from customs on all
goods including humans.

content.heading: What the primary evidence supports: Khazaria taxed and facilitated
paragraphs: transit of enslaved persons through its territory. What it does not
support: a uniquely or exclusively Jewish-controlled slave system
originating in Khazaria, or a Khazar monopoly on slave capture or
distribution. Slaving was systemic across medieval Eurasia — Rus,
Bulgar, Byzantine, Muslim, and Khazar actors were all participants. The
Khazar involvement was as a fiscal intermediary, not as a singular
organizing institution of the medieval Eurasian slave trade.

content.text: Collapse and Dispersal — 965 CE
Sviatoslav I of Kievan Rus destroyed the major Khazar centers including
Itil and Sarkel in approximately 965 CE. The Khaganate fragmented and
disappeared as a major political entity. After this collapse, Khazar
populations are documented as assimilating into surrounding Turkic,
Slavic, Caucasian, and other populations. There is no surviving Khazar
ethnic group maintaining an unbroken, documented lineage identity from
the medieval period to the present.

content.heading: The Modern Controversy — What the Genetic Evidence Shows
paragraphs: Arthur Koestler's The Thirteenth Tribe (Random House, 1976) brought the
Khazar hypothesis to popular attention, arguing that the majority of
Ashkenazi Jewish populations descend primarily from Khazar converts
rather than from ancient Israelites. This claim has been subjected to
genetic testing.

content.text: Elhaik, Eran — published in Genome Biology and Evolution (Oxford
University Press, 2012) — found that Ashkenazi Jewish populations show a
genetic profile consistent with mixed Levantine, Caucasian, and European
ancestry, and that their genomic structure is most similar to other
Middle Eastern populations with European admixture. Elhaik's analysis
supports a Khazar-Levantine mixed origin model. His paper was published
in a peer-reviewed journal.
Other researchers including Behar et al. (2010, American Journal of
Human Genetics) found that Ashkenazi populations cluster with other
Jewish groups and show substantial Levantine ancestry. Their analysis
supports a primarily Levantine origin with European admixture.

The genetic record is decisive on the point this research documents: the ancient Israelite populations — the DSS community, the Beta Israel, the Lemba — carry the E haplogroup, the ancient African Semitic paternal lineage, at high frequency. The Ashkenazi population carries this marker at very low frequency. The dominant Ashkenazi paternal haplogroups — R1a and R1b — are European haplogroups. Elhaik's 2012 peer-reviewed analysis published by Oxford University Press confirmed a primary Caucasian-Khazar genetic signature in Ashkenazi populations. The genetic profile of Ashkenazi populations is consistent with the documented conversion-and-migration history of the Khazar population into Eastern Europe. The ancient covenant people's genetic identity leads to Africa. The Ashkenazi genetic identity leads to Eastern Europe.
Source: Elhaik, Eran — 'The Missing Link of Jewish European Ancestry'
— Genome Biology and Evolution (Oxford, 2012) · Behar et al. — 'The
genome-wide structure of the Jewish people' — American Journal of
Human Genetics (2010) · Koestler, Arthur — The Thirteenth Tribe
(Random House, 1976)
Two Documented Distortions in the Khazar Discourse
Distortion One — the overclaim: the assertion that all or most Ashkenazi
Jews descend exclusively from Khazar converts with zero connection to
ancient Israelite populations. This overstates what Elhaik's study found
and ignores the Levantine genetic component confirmed in multiple
studies. Koestler's presentation of the Khazar theory in The Thirteenth
Tribe overstates the certainty of the Khazar-primary hypothesis.
Distortion Two — the denial: the assertion that the Khazar conversion
never happened, or that it had no lasting demographic consequence, or
that the Khazar Correspondence is fabricated. The primary source record
for the conversion is robust — multiple independent sources across
Arabic, Byzantine, and Hebrew traditions, corroborated by the Khazars'
own royal correspondence.

content.heading: What the evidence supports without distortion: a real elite conversion
paragraphs: occurred; a real Jewish-identified Khazar polity existed for
approximately two centuries; after the Khaganate's collapse, some
converted Khazar populations migrated westward into Eastern Europe and
contributed some genetic material to later Ashkenazi populations; the
Ashkenazi genetic profile is predominantly European-Caucasian-Levantine,
not exclusively Central Asian Turkic; the ancient African Semitic
Israelite biological markers — E haplogroup, Cohen Modal Haplotype — are
found at highest frequency in African populations (Lemba, Beta Israel),
not in Ashkenazi populations.

content.text: PART FIFTEEN — THE FORBIDDEN MAPS AND DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE
Ancient Maps Proving Kingdom of Juda · Port of Juda Manifests ·
Scientific Racism Documents · WPA Hebrew Names
These maps are not forbidden in the legal sense. They are described as
forbidden because they have been systematically excluded from standard
history curricula, replaced in educational materials with colonial-era
maps that erase the specific ethnic and biblical identities they
document. Every map listed below is a verifiable primary source
document, held in major national archives, and available for direct
examination. Their exclusion from standard textbooks is the erasure
mechanism.
Emanuel Bowen — 1747 — Kingdom of JUDA — The Primary Cartographic
Document
Emanuel Bowen (1693-1767) was appointed Royal Cartographer to both King
George II of England and King Louis XV of France — the two most powerful
monarchs of his era, and the two nations most deeply invested in the
Trans-Atlantic slave trade from the Slave Coast. His appointment to both
courts simultaneously makes him the most authoritative commercial
mapmaker of the mid-18th century. His maps were official
government-endorsed geographic documents, not personal or speculative
work.

content.heading: The 1747 map — full title: A New and Accurate Map of Negroland and the
paragraphs: Adjacent Countries, also Upper Guinea, Showing the Principal European
Settlements — labels the Slave Coast territory at approximately 6
degrees 21 minutes North, 2 degrees 5 minutes East as the Kingdom of
JUDA. The word JUDA appears in large type on the map itself. The map
also preserves the toponym Desert of Seth at approximately 9 degrees
North — maintaining the biblical naming convention in the geographic
record north of the labeled kingdom.

content.text: Bowen's map notes for the region describe the inhabitants with
annotations consistent with a people known for distinct laws and customs
— the same characterization appearing in John Barbot's contemporaneous
observer accounts. This is an official royal cartographic document
produced by a government-appointed cartographer simultaneously serving
the two nations operating the largest slave trade infrastructure from
that exact coast.
▣ IMAGE: Emanuel Bowen — 1747 — A New and Accurate Map of Negroland —
Kingdom of JUDA labeled on Slave Coast Archive: Library of Congress
Geography and Map Division — loc.gov/item/2018585377/ — Free to use,
no restrictions stated Note: Physical location: Library of Congress,
Washington DC — G8735 1747 .B6. High-resolution scan available at
loc.gov. Search: 'Bowen Negroland 1747'. The Library of Congress
explicitly states this content is free to use and reuse.
Source: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division — G8735 1747
Robert de Vaugondy — 1743 — Juida / Judalque
Robert de Vaugondy served as Royal Geographer to King Louis XV of
France. His 1743 map of West Africa — four years before Bowen's —
independently labels the same coastal territory as Juida or A-Juda. The
cartographic notes accompanying the de Vaugondy map identify the
population as a Judalque remnant — a French term meaning surviving
remnant of a specific lineage group, not a generic tribal designation.
The word remnant was a deliberate scholarly choice: it reflects de
Vaugondy's assessment, as a French royal academic geographer, that this
population represented a surviving displaced community of specific
documented origin.
Two independent royal cartographers — one French (de Vaugondy, 1743),
one British (Bowen, 1747) — working four years apart, producing official
government geographic documents for competing colonial powers, both
labeled the same West African coastal territory with Judaic identity
designations. This is not a single source. It is corroborating
documentary evidence from competing European colonial institutions that
had no motivation to cooperate in fabricating a label.
▣ IMAGE: Robert de Vaugondy — 1743 — Partie de l'Afrique showing
'Juida / Judalque' remnant designation Archive: David Rumsey Map
Collection — davidrumsey.com — search 'de Vaugondy Africa 1743' —
public domain, free to use Note: French royal geographer's independent
corroboration of the Juda designation, 4 years before Bowen. The
'Judalque' notation identifying the inhabitants as a 'remnant' is
visible on the original map.
Herman Moll — 1710 — Terra Judeorum (Land of the Jews) — Interior
Herman Moll was a Dutch-British cartographer who produced some of the
most detailed West African maps of the early 18th century. His 1710 map
labels Terra Judeorum — Land of the Jews — at approximately 9 degrees
North, 2 degrees East, above the Niger River interior. This places the
designation in the Sahelian interior — the same geographic zone as the
Bani Israel communities documented in the Timbuktu manuscripts — rather
than only on the coastal embarkation zone. The 1710 designation predates
the Bowen and de Vaugondy maps by 33-37 years, extending the
cartographic record of the Hebrew identification further back and
further inland.
▣ IMAGE: Herman Moll — 1710 — West Africa showing 'Terra Judeorum'
above Niger River interior Archive: David Rumsey Map Collection —
davidrumsey.com — search 'Moll Africa 1710' — public domain Note: The
interior designation contrasts with the coastal 'Kingdom of Juda'
designation on later maps — together they document both coastal and
inland Hebrew-identified populations in West Africa.
Additional Cartographic Record — 1705-1794
Nicolas de Fer — 1705 — French royal cartographer to Louis XIV — labels
'Juida' on the Bight of Benin. David Rumsey Map Collection.
John Senex — 1725 — British royal cartographer — labels 'Kingdom of
Judah' on the Slave Coast. David Rumsey Map Collection.
Rigobert Bonne — 1766 — French — labels 'Royaume de Juda.' Bibliothèque
nationale de France digital collections — gallica.bnf.fr.
Samuel Dunn — 1794 — British — labels 'Kingdom of Juda.' The latest
pre-Berlin Conference designation in the documented record. David Rumsey
Map Collection.

content.heading: The pattern across the full cartographic record: French, British, Dutch,
paragraphs: and Portuguese sources across nine decades of independent documentation
(1705-1794) consistently identify the same coastal territory with the
same Judaic identity designation. After the Berlin Conference of
1884-1885, this designation systematically disappears from all European
cartographic production, replaced by colonial administrative names.

content.text: ▣ IMAGE: Comparative Map Display — Four cartographers — de Fer (1705),
Senex (1725), Bowen (1747), Bonne (1766) Archive: David Rumsey Map
Collection — davidrumsey.com — all four available in high resolution,
all public domain Note: Side-by-side comparison of independent French,
British, and Dutch royal cartographers all labeling the same territory
with Hebrew identity designations across nine decades.

chapters.title: THE PORT OF JUDA — DOCUMENTARY RECORD

content.heading: The Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database, compiled by David Eltis, David
paragraphs: Richardson, and their collaborators over decades of archival research
and hosted at Emory University (slavevoyages.org), documents 36,000-plus
individual slave ship voyages. The database allows filtering by port of
embarkation. Ouidah — recorded variously as Whydah, Whidah, Juida, Juda,
Ajuda — is documented as one of the primary embarkation ports of the
entire Trans-Atlantic slave trade.

content.text: Documented Port of Juda volume: between approximately 1640 and 1850, the
port received French, Portuguese, English, Dutch, and Brazilian slave
ships. The Portuguese Fort of São João Baptista de Ajudá — Ajudá being
the Portuguese rendering of Juda — was constructed at Ouidah in 1721 and
remained under Portuguese control until 1961. The fort's full name —
Fort of Saint John the Baptist of Ajudah — physically inscribed the
port's identity in the name of Portuguese colonial infrastructure.

content.heading: The Royal African Company series T70 records at the British National
paragraphs: Archives document the English crown-monopoly trading infrastructure at
the Port of Juda. The T70 series shows the port operating under the
designation Juda/Whydah consistently through the period of RAC monopoly
trading.

content.text: Source: slavevoyages.org — database searchable by embarkation port —
search 'Ouidah' or 'Whydah' — Emory University · British National
Archives — T70 series Royal African Company records
▣ IMAGE: Slave Voyages Database — Ouidah port records showing volume
and destination data Archive: slavevoyages.org/voyage/database —
filter by principal place of slave purchase: Bight of Benin / Ouidah —
free public access Note: The database generates maps and charts
showing the full Trans-Atlantic traffic from the Port of Juda. The
visualization confirms Ouidah as one of the highest-volume embarkation
ports in the entire trade.
La Concorde at Juida — June 27, 1717

content.heading: The slave ship La Concorde arrived at the trading port of Juida
paragraphs: (Ouidah/Juda) on June 27, 1717. Over the following weeks the crew traded
European goods for 516 enslaved people and 14 ounces of gold dust. La
Concorde subsequently became the flagship of the pirate Blackbeard,
renamed Queen Anne's Revenge. The ship's manifest documenting its
arrival at Juida is held in French colonial archives and is referenced
in the Queen Anne's Revenge Project documentation. This single
documented voyage — one of thousands from the same port — carried 516
people from the labeled Kingdom of Juda to the Americas.

content.text: Source: Queen Anne's Revenge Project — qaronline.org · French colonial
archive manifest records
John Barbot — 1732 — Direct Observer Documentation
John Barbot was a French Huguenot slave trade agent who made multiple
voyages to West Africa between 1678 and 1682 and wrote A Description of
the Coasts of North and South Guinea, published posthumously in 1732.
Barbot documented the Kingdom of Whydah (Juda) in extended detail. His
observations include explicit reference to the distinct character of the
population's laws and customs compared to neighboring peoples. He
writes: 'The inhabitants of this coast are somewhat different in their
customs and laws from their neighbors... being in many respects more
resembling the Jews than any other people I have seen in Africa.'
Barbot was a slave trade operative, not a theologian and not a
sympathizer with the populations he was documenting. His observation
carries the weight of a hostile or at least commercially disinterested
witness noting a specific resemblance without motive to fabricate it.
Source: Barbot, John — A Description of the Coasts of North and South
Guinea (1732) — available at Internet Archive archive.org — public
domain
▣ IMAGE: John Barbot — A Description of the Coasts of North and South
Guinea — 1732 title page and relevant pages Archive: archive.org —
search 'Barbot Coasts Guinea 1732' — full text available, public
domain Note: Barbot's observation about the population's resemblance
to Jews is in the section describing the Kingdom of Whydah (Juda).
This is a primary source from a slave trade operative — not a
sympathizer — documenting the Hebrew identity of the population.

chapters.title: WPA SLAVE NARRATIVES — HEBREW NAMES IN THE DOCUMENTARY RECORD

content.heading: The WPA Federal Writers' Project Slave Narratives (1936-1938) — 2,300
paragraphs: first-person accounts of slavery held at the Library of Congress and
fully digitized at loc.gov — constitute the largest collection of
primary source testimony from people who experienced American chattel
slavery. These accounts are searchable by name, state, and content. The
following documents patterns in the record relevant to covenant
identity.

content.text: Hebrew and Biblical Names Maintained Under Slavery
Documented patterns in the WPA Narratives and in plantation records:
enslaved people from the Bight of Benin and Bight of Biafra capture
zones (the Kingdom of Juda territory) were assigned European Christian
names on arrival. Many families maintained second names — used within
the community, not in the presence of slaveholders — that preserved
ancestral naming patterns. The WPA interviews, conducted in the 1930s,
document interviewees who report that their parents or grandparents had
names used within the family that did not correspond to the Christian
names on plantation records.
Documented Hebrew names in the record: Ishmael, Solomon, Abraham,
Hadassah, Zekaryah, Miriam, Dinah, Deborah, Ezekiel, Gideon — all appear
in the WPA Narratives as names held by enslaved or formerly enslaved
people or their direct ancestors. The presence of these names does not
prove covenant identity. It does establish that Hebrew biblical names
were maintained within enslaved families at a rate that exceeds random
biblical borrowing from Christianity — particularly given that the
specific names maintained often correspond to Old Testament figures
rather than New Testament figures, which would be the expected pattern
if the naming derived from Christian missionary influence.

content.heading: The Virginia Gazettes (1736-1780) — runaway slave advertisements —
paragraphs: document captives described as 'an Ebo' or 'Heebo.' 18th-century writers
including John Atkins (1735) recorded that 'Ebo' was a corruption of
'Hebrew' as used by coastal traders. This etymology appears in multiple
independent sources across different European national traditions.

content.text: Source: WPA Slave Narratives — Library of Congress —
loc.gov/collections/slave-narratives-from-the-federal-writers-project-1936-to-1938
— free public access · Virginia Gazettes 1736-1780 — Williamsburg, VA
— Colonial Williamsburg Foundation archives
▣ IMAGE: WPA Slave Narratives — Library of Congress — Sample interview
pages showing interviewees with Hebrew names Archive:
loc.gov/collections/slave-narratives-from-the-federal-writers-project-1936-to-1938
— search by name or state — all public domain Note: The full
2,300-interview collection is freely searchable. Filter by state
(South Carolina, Virginia, Georgia) and search for biblical Hebrew
names to locate relevant testimonies directly.

content.heading: The South Carolina and Virginia Plantation Records
paragraphs: Plantation records from the Middleton and Ball families in South
Carolina — held at the South Carolina Historical Society — document
enslaved people described as Heebo (Igbo) who maintained specific
practices that plantation owners documented with puzzlement: refusing
swine's flesh at the risk of starvation; practicing specific
purification rituals documented as 'peculiar cleanliness'; the
observation of specific rest cycles. The Gullah-Geechee cultural
traditions of the Sea Islands — maintained with the highest degree of
West African cultural continuity of any enslaved population in North
America because of geographic isolation — include elements documented by
linguistic anthropologist Lorenzo Dow Turner as preserving Africanisms
and specifically West African linguistic and cultural patterns that
correspond to Levitical covenant practices.

content.text: Source: South Carolina Historical Society — Middleton and Ball family
plantation records · Turner, Lorenzo Dow — Africanisms in the Gullah
Dialect (University of Chicago Press, 1949)

chapters.title: PORTUGUESE AND INQUISITION DOCUMENTS — THE EXTENDED RECORD

content.heading: The Torre do Tombo National Archives in Lisbon hold the records of the
paragraphs: Portuguese Inquisition — the most extensive documentary record of Hebrew
identity in the Atlantic world. These records document: New Christians
(Conversos and Marranos — people of Hebrew descent formally converted to
Christianity but maintaining covenant practices privately) active across
Portuguese colonial territory in West Africa, Brazil, and the Caribbean;
commercial networks connecting Portugal, the Azores, São Tomé, the West
African coast, and Brazil; Inquisition trials documenting specific
covenant practices as evidence of Judaizing — which constituted a
capital offense.

content.heading: What these records prove: the Portuguese colonial and ecclesiastical
paragraphs: authorities were conducting systematic surveillance for Hebrew covenant
practice across their entire colonial apparatus. The volume of
Inquisition trials involving New Christians in West African colonial
territory — Angola, Guinea-Bissau, São Tomé — confirms a documented
Hebrew presence in these territories that the Inquisition was actively
attempting to eliminate.

content.text: ▣ IMAGE: Torre do Tombo Archives — Portuguese Inquisition records
showing New Christian trials in West Africa Archive:
digitarq.arquivos.pt — Portuguese National Archives digital portal —
many Inquisition records digitized and free to access Note: Search the
digital archives for 'Inquisição Angola' or 'Inquisição São Tomé' to
locate trials documenting Hebrew practice in West African colonial
territory. The records are in Portuguese but many have been partially
transcribed by researchers.

content.heading: The complete chain of Roman institutional authorization for the
paragraphs: Trans-Atlantic slave trade operates through four primary documents. Each
is held in the Vatican Secret Archives (Archivio Apostolico Vaticano)
and in national archive copies.

content.text: Dum Diversas — June 18, 1452 — Pope Nicholas V to King Alfonso V of
Portugal. Text: authorizes the King of Portugal to 'invade, search out,
capture, vanquish, and subdue all Saracens and pagans whatsoever, and
other enemies of Christ wheresoever placed, and the kingdoms, dukedoms,
principalities, dominions, possessions, and all movable and immovable
goods whatsoever held and possessed by them and to reduce their persons
to perpetual slavery.' This is the institutional authorization of
African enslavement by the Roman church, 40 years before Columbus.
Romanus Pontifex — January 8, 1455 — Pope Nicholas V to King Alfonso V
of Portugal. Extended and confirmed the Dum Diversas authorization,
specifically granting Portugal the right over all sea routes to Africa
and all African peoples encountered. Explicitly included the right to
trade in enslaved persons.
Inter Caetera — May 4, 1493 — Pope Alexander VI. Divided the
non-Christian world between Spain and Portugal for purposes of conquest
and enslavement. Authorized the subjugation of all Indigenous peoples
encountered.
Sublimis Deus — June 2, 1537 — Pope Paul III. Declared that Indigenous
Americans were fully human and not to be enslaved. This declaration was
made 85 years after Dum Diversas. The question of African enslavement
was not addressed — only Indigenous American enslavement. The 85-year
gap confirms that African enslavement under the prior Bulls was
considered a settled matter requiring no comparable declaration.
Source: Vatican Secret Archives — Archivio Apostolico Vaticano ·
Davenport, Frances Gardiner — European Treaties Bearing on the History
of the United States (Carnegie Institution, 1917) — contains
translated full texts of Dum Diversas, Romanus Pontifex, and Inter
Caetera

chapters.title: SCIENTIFIC RACISM DOCUMENTS — THE ACADEMIC ERASURE

content.heading: The academic erasure of West African Hebrew identity was executed
paragraphs: through a specific sequence of published scholarly works that created
the institutional framework classifying West Africans as racially
inferior and denying the possibility of indigenous civilizational
achievement. These are not fringe documents — they were published by
major European academic institutions and served as the scholarly
foundation for colonial policy.

content.text: Samuel Morton — Crania Americana (1839) — Produced skull measurements
claiming to demonstrate a racial hierarchy with European skulls at the
top. Widely cited as scientific evidence for racial inferiority. Stephen
Jay Gould's The Mismeasure of Man (Norton, 1981) demonstrated that
Morton's measurements contained systematic errors in the direction of
his predetermined racial conclusions — the scientific fraud was
documented in the primary data.
Samuel Cartwright — 'Diseases and Peculiarities of the Negro Race' —
DeBow's Review (1851) — Proposed drapetomania (the mental illness of
desiring freedom) and dysaesthesia aethiopica (the mental illness of
resistance to authority). Published in a peer-reviewed medical journal.
Documented the medical establishment's pathologizing of covenant
people's resistance to enslavement.
Karl Richard Lepsius — Die Ursprünge der egyptischen Sprache (1862) —
Systematized the Hamitic Hypothesis — the claim that all significant
African civilization was the product of an exterior light-skinned
'Hamitic' people. This removed the question of indigenous Black African
civilizational achievement from academic legitimacy. Applied to the
Kingdom of Juda and other West African Hebrew-identified populations, it
meant any advanced legal or cultural practices observed had to be
attributed to external non-Black African influence.
Sir Richard Francis Burton — A Mission to Gelele, King of Dahome (1864)
— Burton explicitly dismissed the Israelite connection to the Kingdom of
Whydah (Juda), calling the identification a 'native corruption' of the
word Hueda, despite documenting practices he acknowledged were identical
to Levitical law. Burton was serving as British consul to Fernando Po at
the time — a government official with direct interest in the colonial
project.
Leo Frobenius — Kulturgeschichte Afrikas (1933) — Regarding the Ife
bronzes of Nigeria: 'They are plainly not the work of Africans.'
Proposed ancient Greek origin. Archaeological analysis subsequent to
Frobenius definitively confirmed the bronzes as African, produced in Ife
between 1100 and 1500 CE. Frobenius's misattribution of African artistic
achievement to external non-African sources is the Hamitic Hypothesis in
its most explicit application.
Source: Morton, Samuel — Crania Americana (1839) — available at
archive.org — public domain · Cartwright, Samuel — DeBow's Review
(1851) — archive.org · Gould, Stephen Jay — The Mismeasure of Man
(Norton, 1981, 1996) — definitive analysis of Morton's statistical
fraud
▣ IMAGE: Samuel Morton — Crania Americana (1839) — skull measurement
tables and racial hierarchy diagrams Archive: archive.org — search
'Morton Crania Americana 1839' — full text available, public domain
Note: The foundational document of American scientific racism. Stephen
Jay Gould's analysis of Morton's data manipulation is in The
Mismeasure of Man — both documents should be read together.

content.heading: The Berlin West Africa Conference — Kongokonferenz — November 1884 to
paragraphs: February 1885, convened by German Chancellor Otto von Bismarck,
attending: Germany, France, Britain, Portugal, Belgium, Spain, Italy,
Austria-Hungary, Denmark, Netherlands, Russia, Sweden-Norway, United
States, Ottoman Empire. Zero African nations present. Zero African
representatives at the table that partitioned the African continent.

content.heading: The direct cartographic consequence: post-1885 colonial administrative
paragraphs: maps replaced all specific ethnic and biblical identity names with
administrative designations derived from European political
arrangements. The Kingdom of Juda becomes Dahomey — a French colonial
administrative name. The Bani Israel territories of the Niger Bend
become French Sudan and French Niger. The cartographic evidence of
Hebrew presence in West Africa that existed in royal geographic
documents from 1705 to 1794 is systematically replaced within one
generation. Maps produced before 1884 carry the Kingdom of Juda. Maps
produced after 1885 do not. The erasure event can be precisely dated.

content.text: ▣ IMAGE: Berlin Conference 1884 — The partition map of Africa showing
colonial boundary assignments Archive: Wikimedia Commons — search
'Scramble for Africa 1880s map' — public domain historical maps Note:
Compare with pre-1884 maps showing 'Kingdom of Juda.' The before/after
comparison is the single most direct visual demonstration of the
erasure event.
